issue.body:
Due to the following bug in Netty: https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/6770

It seems like the connection is closed. An exception will be logged by Netty, which is potentially expensive. It's probably OK to leave it as it is, but we should keep track of this.

```
05:53:55.405 [armeria-server-boss-epoll-26-1] WARN  io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel - Failed to close a channel.
java.lang.IllegalStateException: channel not registered to an event loop
	at io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel.eventLoop(AbstractChannel.java:158)
	at io.netty.channel.epoll.AbstractEpollChannel.doDeregister(AbstractEpollChannel.java:140)
	at io.netty.channel.epoll.AbstractEpollChannel.doClose(AbstractEpollChannel.java:117)
	at io.netty.channel.epoll.AbstractEpollStreamChannel.doClose(AbstractEpollStreamChannel.java:721)
	at io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel$AbstractUnsafe.closeForcibly(AbstractChannel.java:703)
```

body: Epoll only. By the way, the connection seems to be closed because `socket.close()` is in the `finally` block. It raises an exception while trying to deregister.

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
…istered before.

Motivation:

We only can call eventLoop() if we are registered on an EventLoop yet. As we just did this without checking we spammed the log with an error that was harmless.

Modifications:

Check if registered on eventLoop before try to deregister on close.

Result:

Fixes [#6770]

body: To clarify ... the issue is an exception is thrown, not that the channel isn't closed, correct?
We need to deregister the channel to ensure the state of the EventLoop is correctly updated. Seems safe to ignore (or not generate) an expiation if the EventLoop is null in this case.
